title: The Tripitaka and the Dhammapada

explain.say: The Tripitaka is the oldest collection of Buddhist scriptures. Its name means three baskets, perhaps because the teachings were once written on palm leaves and kept in baskets, and its Pali version is called the Pali Canon.

items: Vinaya Pitaka: rules for monks and nuns
Abhidhamma Pitaka: deeper analysis of mind

draw.text: In Pali: Tipitaka. Sacred to Theravada Buddhists

explain.say: The teachings go back to the Buddha, who lived in north India around the 5th century BCE. He was born at Lumbini, awakened at Bodh Gaya, gave his first teaching at Sarnath and died at Kushinagar.

draw.text: Born, awakened, first taught, passed away

explain.say: After the Buddha died, tradition says his followers met at a council and recited his teachings together: Ananda recited the discourses and Upali the monastic rules. For centuries they were passed on by memory, then written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE.

items: About 5th century BCE: the Buddha teaches
Soon after: first council recites the teachings
3rd century BCE: Buddhism reaches Sri Lanka
1st century BCE: Pali Canon written on palm leaves

draw.text: Recited by memory for about four centuries

explain.say: The middle basket, the Sutta Pitaka, holds thousands of the Buddha's talks, including the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path, the way to end suffering.

draw.text: The Four Noble Truths: suffering, its cause, its end, the path

explain.say: The Dhammapada is a much loved book of the Sutta Pitaka: 423 short verses of the Buddha's sayings in 26 chapters. It teaches that our minds shape our lives, and that hatred is never ended by hatred, only by love.

draw.value: Hatred is never ended by hatred, but by non-hatred alone. This is an eternal law.
draw.label: Dhammapada, verse 5, a common rendering

explain.say: Other Buddhist traditions have their own large canons: Mahayana schools in China, Korea and Japan read sutras such as the Lotus Sutra and Heart Sutra, and Tibetan Buddhists have the Kangyur.

items: Theravada | Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand | Pali Canon
Mahayana | China, Korea, Japan, Vietnam | Chinese canon, Lotus Sutra
Vajrayana | Tibet, Bhutan, Mongolia | Kangyur and Tengyur

faq.a: The Tripitaka, or Tipitaka in Pali, is the oldest collection of Buddhist scriptures. Its name means three baskets: the Vinaya, rules for monks and nuns; the Suttas, the Buddha's discourses; and the Abhidhamma, a detailed analysis of mind and experience.
The three baskets are the Vinaya Pitaka, the discipline for monks and nuns; the Sutta Pitaka, the Buddha's talks; and the Abhidhamma Pitaka, which analyses the mind and reality in detail.
asks: What is in the three baskets of Buddhism?

faq.a: The Pali Canon is the Tripitaka in the Pali language, the scripture of Theravada Buddhism, followed in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia. It is the most complete early Buddhist canon that survives in an Indian language.
asks: What language is the Tripitaka in?
Which Buddhists use the Pali Canon?

faq.a: The teachings come from the Buddha and his early disciples. Tradition says they were recited at a council soon after his death, with Ananda reciting the discourses and Upali the rules, and passed down by memory before being written down.
asks: Did the Buddha write the Tripitaka?

faq.q: When was the Tripitaka written down?
faq.a: The Pali Canon was passed down by memory for centuries and, according to Sri Lankan chronicles, first written on palm leaves in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE.
asks: How old are the Buddhist scriptures?
When were the Buddha's teachings written?
Where was the Pali Canon written down?

faq.a: The Dhammapada is a collection of 423 verses of the Buddha's sayings in 26 chapters, part of the Sutta Pitaka. Its short, memorable lines on the mind, kindness and wisdom make it one of the best known Buddhist texts.
asks: How many verses are in the Dhammapada?
Is the Dhammapada part of the Tripitaka?

faq.a: It teaches that the mind shapes our lives: speak or act with a pure mind and happiness follows. It also says hatred is ended not by hatred but by love, and that conquering yourself is greater than conquering thousands in battle.
asks: What is the message of the Dhammapada?
What does the Buddha say about hatred?

faq.a: The Sutta Pitaka is the basket of the Buddha's discourses, thousands of talks given to monks, nuns and lay people. It is arranged in five collections, called nikayas, and includes the first sermon on the Four Noble Truths.
The Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules of discipline for Buddhist monks and nuns, with the stories of why each rule was made. Monks and nuns still recite its core rules regularly in their communities.
asks: What are the rules for Buddhist monks?

faq.a: The Abhidhamma Pitaka is the third basket, a careful analysis of the mind, feelings and experience into their smallest parts. It is often seen as Buddhist philosophy and psychology.

faq.q: Do all Buddhists use the Tripitaka?
faq.a: Theravada Buddhists use the Pali Tripitaka. Mahayana Buddhists in East Asia have a large Chinese canon with sutras like the Lotus Sutra and the Heart Sutra, and Tibetan Buddhists have the Kangyur and Tengyur.
asks: What scriptures do Mahayana Buddhists use?

faq.q: Why is it called three baskets?
faq.a: Pitaka means basket. One common explanation is that the palm leaf manuscripts of each section were kept in separate baskets, or that the teachings were handed on like baskets passed from person to person.
asks: Where does the name Tripitaka come from?

faq.q: Where is the Tripitaka carved in stone?
faq.a: At the Kuthodaw Pagoda in Mandalay, Myanmar, the whole Tripitaka was carved on 729 marble slabs in the 1860s, each in its own small shrine. It is often called the world's largest book.
asks: What is the world's largest book?
Is there a Buddhist book made of stone?

facts: The Tripitaka, or three baskets, is made of the Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitakas.
The Pali Canon was first written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE, after centuries of oral recitation.
The Dhammapada has 423 verses in 26 chapters and is part of the Sutta Pitaka.
The Sutta Pitaka is arranged in five collections called nikayas.
At the Kuthodaw Pagoda in Mandalay, the Tripitaka is carved on 729 marble slabs.

quiz.say: Which basket of the Tripitaka contains the rules for monks and nuns?
quiz.show: Which basket holds the rules for monks and nuns?
quiz.why: Vinaya means discipline; this basket holds the monastic rules and the stories behind them.

wrong.1: The Sutta Pitaka holds the Buddha's discourses, his talks.
wrong.2: The Abhidhamma Pitaka analyses mind and experience in detail.

quiz.say: Two friends have a quarrel, and one wants to get revenge. Which teaching of the Dhammapada fits best?
quiz.show: Which Dhammapada teaching fits a quarrel?

options.show: Hatred is ended by love, not hatred
options.say: Hatred is ended by love, not by hatred

quiz.why: Verse 5 of the Dhammapada teaches that hatred is never ended by hatred but only by non-hatred, or love.

wrong.1: The Dhammapada values self-mastery over winning against others.
wrong.2: Cutting everyone off is not its teaching; it encourages kindness and wise speech.

quiz.say: The Buddha's teachings were passed on by memory for about four hundred years before being written down. What helped this work?
quiz.show: How were the teachings kept for 400 years without writing?

options.say: Communities of monks reciting together, with lots of repetition

quiz.why: Monks recited the teachings together and the texts use repetition and lists, which make them easier to memorise and check.

wrong.2: They were remembered well enough to be written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE.
